issues.problem:
The suite does not see most mutants of round 5's own lines.

What I ran (m2x-v1-6/mutate6.py, results in out/mutants6.json):
- 136 line mutants of Cover.luau 568-570, 580-605, 613-632, 641-678 and 937-952, plus 22 hand mutants.
- Each ran against `lune run tests/run -- --quick --root tests/Physics`, with the case budget raised to 60 s.
- 117 were killed and 41 survived.

Why so many survive: every search the suite runs is against one disk along world Z, centred at x = z = 0. That holds for both the tilted case and the pucks sword in Verdict.spec.

20 of the survivors change behaviour:

(i) Seven break the search's frame or bounds for any host oriented another way. Each is an identity when the host's axis is (0, 0, ±1):
- 582: `ny / uz`, which gives inf or NaN for a host along X or Y.
- 582: `ny * uz + nz * uy`.
- 589: the sign of `ey * uy` in `eu`.
- 619: `mx / P.vx` in pv.
- 629: the sign of `wy * uy` in `wu`.
- 630: `mx - r * (...)` in the lower bound's point, which is then no point of the circle.
- 660: the sign of `dy * uy` in `along`.

(ii) Two raise the parallel cutoff, to 1e-3 or 0.03. rimFarthest then takes the axes as parallel up to that tilt and answers |m| + r. That is r·(1 − cos θ) above the rim: up to 5e-7·r at 1e-3, i.e. 4e-7 for r 0.8, which is past EPS_GEOM. So a rod truly within the coincident band reads as poking out.
The suite cannot see this:
- its smallest non-zero tilt from the disk's axis is 2° (0.035 rad);
- at a near-axial tilt toward the tangent, the bounds agree and no cap is ever searched.

(iii) Ten change what a search is charged, and no test counts it. The suite asserts only `used ∈ {0.5, 28.5, 56.5}` per held reading and `searched > 0`:
- the second open cap charged nothing;
- one 28 charged however many caps are open;
- bounds that leave more caps open: the upper bound 1e-3 high; the lower bound 1e-9 low; the lower bound taken from the circle point away from p, or from a turned point; `pl > 1`; and three mangled lines `c, sn = …`.

(iv) One drops the rule-A loop's report (947, `if due()` → `if false`). A puck against 20 nearly coincident disks then reports 570 units at once. That breaks §4.9's "a report carries 256 units and one step of work at most", and no case has a run of searched tests.

The other 21 survivors are equivalent or only act at a tie:
- cutoffs from 1e-12 to 1e-4, and `<` for `<=` (error at most 5e-9·r below 1e-4);
- 15 to 30 halvings (error at most about 1e-10);
- `held` with `<`;
- the cut branch's return, which is reached only at ties: below 1e-8 the bounds lie within r²·1e-16;
- `lo = -2`, `>=` for `>`, and state 2 for 1;
- the default point and the NaN path when p = 0, where the upper bound is exact;
- the two returns after the budget is passed.
One pre-existing `along` line also survives (658, `P.cx + Q.cx`): no case puts a part near a hider's cap with the hider off x = 0.

The build itself is right: my 50-digit check and my brute force (verified) agree with it at every host frame. The tests are what is weak, and the round's text says "12 mutants … all killed".
issues.fix:
Tried in m2x-v1-6/tfix6. The full diff is m2x-v1-6/out/tfix6_cover_spec.diff (146 lines, tests only).

1. Factor the tilted case into `local function tiltedRods(T: { number }, c: { number }, turns: { { number } }): (number, number, number, number)`.
- The disk: `Shapes.prepare(H.solid(1, "Cylinder", c, Quat.hemisphere(Quat.normalize(Quat.mul(T, H.Y90))), { 0.5, 2 * R, 2 * R }, "Guard"), 1)`.
- Each turn {turn, lean}: `q0 = Quat.hemisphere(Quat.normalize(Quat.mul(H.axisAngle(-ry, rx, 0, lean), Quat.mul(H.axisAngle(rx, ry, 0, turn), H.axisAngle(0, 0, 1, math.deg(math.atan2(-rx, ry)))))))`.
- Each rod: rotation `Quat.mul(T, q)`; position c + M(T)·(y0·rx + shift·nx, y0·ry + shift·ny, shift·nz), with M = Quat.toMatrix(T).
- Accumulate `units += used` over every reading, held or not.
- Return checked, held, searched and units.

2. The existing case calls `tiltedRods(H.I, { 0, 2, 0 }, { { 0, 0 }, { 2, 0 }, { 30, 0 }, { 60, 0 }, { 88, 0 }, { 90, 0 } })` and asserts `checked == 720 and held == 360 and searched == 136` and `A.eq(units, 709562, "the readings' units")`.

3. Add a case '(a) … tilted rods in a turned Cylinder, and near its axis':
- `tiltedRods(Quat.hemisphere(Quat.normalize(H.axisAngle(1, 2, 3, 37))), { 0.13, 2.07, -0.11 }, { { 2, 0 }, { 60, 0 }, { 90, 0.03 }, { 90, 0.0046 } })`
- `tiltedRods(H.I, { 0, 2, 0 }, { { 90, 0.03 }, { 90, 0.0046 } })`
- It asserts 480 and 240 checked, 240 and 120 held, 78 and 6 caps searched, and units 478107 and 226227.
- The leans put rods 5.2e-4 and 8e-5 rad off the disk's axis, toward its radius. There the bounds leave caps open, and a parallel cut would stand 1.4e-8 and 3.2e-10 above the rim on a puck, past the 2e-10 margins.

4. Add a case '(f) a run of searched cap rims reports in stretches of SPEND_EVERY and one test':
- 20 Guard disks `{ 0.5, 2R, 2R }`, with R = 0.8 + 1e-7·(k − 1), at (0, 2, 0), rotation H.Y90.
- A Blade puck `{ 0.1, 0.2, 0.2 }` with rotation `Quat.mul(H.axisAngle(-ry, rx, 0, 45), Quat.mul(H.axisAngle(rx, ry, 0, 60), H.axisAngle(0, 0, 1, math.deg(math.atan2(-rx, ry)))))`, placed by 6 secant steps on `Brute.standsOut` against `H.prepare(list[20], 20)` to stand 1e-6 out of the largest disk.
- It asserts: shown > 0; every unit reported; used ≥ 20 × 28.5; largest single report ≤ 512. The build's largest report is 333.625; without the report it is 570 or more.

Results:
- On the build: quick Physics suite 224 pass, 0 fail, 12 skip. `lune run scripts/verify`: VERIFY GREEN, 605 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip, 227.5 s under my own load, luau-lsp passes A and B with 0 errors. New cases take about 0.9, 1.0 and 0.003 s.
- Against the 41 survivors (out/mutants6b.json, out/mutants6c.json): all 20 behaviour-changing ones are killed. Steps 1-4 without the unit pins kill 13; pinning the readings' units kills the 7 lower-bound ones. The 21 equivalent or pre-existing ones remain.

summary:
M2 after fix round 5 passes. One minor issue stands, about test coverage.

**What holds:**
- **Rule A is exact for every pair of round parts, to rounding.** I checked the build's own `lies` against a 50-digit truth of my own, built by a different method from both the build and CoverBrute. All 288,758 decisions agree except within 1.15e-15 of the threshold, at every tilt from 0° to 90°.
- **End to end, the reading matches my brute force.** On 4,650 tangles (18,380 parts), none falls outside the bracket and no value is NaN or inf.
- **The search's cost is charged.** It takes 1,212 ns, about 27 units' time, and is charged 28. It never runs on the plausible set or the attack corpus.
- **Nothing else moved.** Against the tree before round 5, the corpus and a seventh of the plausible set are bit-identical.
- **The texts hold.** I reproduced O9 (b)'s new plate numbers with my own placement: 37.3, 44.1, 47.4 and 48.2-48.3 %, all read 0. The pucks sword plays the truth's row.
- **Invariance, checkpoints, TooComplex and the new-seed VerdictPrecision run all hold.** Orders, mirror images, copies and Dust move nothing. Raised checkpoints leave no state.
- **Checkpoint gaps fit T-PERF-01.** The F, C and X fixtures measure 0.09-0.27 ms, under the 0.35 limit, with the machine 5-7 % busy. I could not check the claim that no run passes 0.26 ms with a forced collection: that run was under up to 30 % load.

**Minor issue:** 41 of 158 mutants of round 5's lines survive the suite. Every rule-A search in the tests runs against one disk along world Z, so 20 of these mutants change behaviour unseen:
- 7 break the search's frame or bounds for any other host orientation;
- 2 raise the parallel cutoff to 1e-3 or 0.03;
- 10 leave the second cap's search uncharged or change which caps are searched;
- 1 drops the rule-A loop's report.

Tests that kill all 20 are tried in m2x-v1-6/tfix6, with verify green at 605/0/0. The remaining 21 survivors are equivalent or act only at a tie.
